context: Traffic recovery session. Blog has 176 published posts; the last ~60 skew heavily toward Claude Code / agent-tooling news, which decays fast and has narrow search demand. This set deliberately rebalances toward high-volume evergreen frontend gaps + one meta post on AI-search visibility.

diagnosis.industryWide: Ahrefs measured a 58% CTR drop on the top-ranking page for keywords with AI Overviews (Feb 2026). Small publishers lost ~60% of search referral traffic over two years; Google referral traffic to publishers fell 38% YoY.
diagnosis.blogSpecific: Topic mix drifted to ephemeral tooling news (Claude Code releases, model reviews) with low evergreen search volume. Verified content gaps with high search demand: React state management, shadcn/ui, Remix 3, browser-native AI, frontend system design.

topics.title: Your Blog Lost 58% of Its Clicks. Here's the GEO Playbook That Actually Works.
topics.whyTrending: Ahrefs measured a 58% CTR reduction on the #1 result for AI Overview keywords in Feb 2026; small publishers are down ~60% over two years and Google referrals to publishers fell 38% YoY. Meanwhile LLM-referred visitors convert at 15.9% (ChatGPT) and 10.5% (Perplexity) vs ~1.76% for organic. Every GEO post out there is marketing fluff — nobody has written the engineer's version: llms.txt, structured data, chunk-level answerability, citation tracking, and what actually gets a technical post quoted by Claude and ChatGPT. Directly self-relevant and highly shareable.
topics.gapNote: Zero coverage on the blog. High volume, evergreen, and the post is its own proof-of-concept.

topics.title: React State Management in 2026: A Decision Tree, Not a Religion
topics.whyTrending: The community finally converged on a clean split — server state (TanStack Query, always), server-owned state (RSC + Server Actions), and a small remainder of client-only UI state (Zustand ~3KB). Redux dropped from 57% to 38% among React Native devs between 2023 and 2026 while Zustand nearly tripled. Real numbers exist: 1000 subscribing components render in 12ms (Zustand), 14ms (Jotai), 18ms (Redux Toolkit), 3ms (signals). This is one of the highest-volume evergreen React queries and the blog has literally zero coverage of it.
topics.gapNote: Biggest evergreen hole in 176 posts. Pairs with existing tanstack-query and RSC posts for internal linking.

topics.title: Remix 3 Threw Out React. Six Weeks With the Beta.
topics.whyTrending: Remix 3 beta preview (April 30, 2026) drops React entirely — no virtual DOM, no build-time magic, a forked Preact underneath, JSX with explicit updates instead of hooks. There is no migration path from Remix v2, whose good parts were folded into React Router v7 instead. Stable targeted for early 2026 and still not production ready. The takes online are all reactions to the announcement; nobody has actually built something and reported back. Controversial, high-volume, and the blog has no Remix 3 coverage at all.
topics.gapNote: Zero coverage. Natural companion to the existing Next.js vs Astro decision posts.

topics.title: shadcn/ui Became a Distribution System. Registries, registry:base and Agent Skills.
topics.whyTrending: CLI v4 (March 2026) lets a registry ship an entire design system as one payload via registry:base — components, deps, CSS vars, fonts and config in a single install. May 2026 added registry include for composing large registries from multiple registry.json files, plus registry validate for pre-publish checks. Base UI is now the default primitive, and shadcn/skills feeds coding agents the context they need to use components and registries correctly. The docs describe the features; nobody has written the 'ship your company's design system as a private registry' walkthrough.
topics.gapNote: Huge search volume, zero coverage. Links naturally to the atomic design and design-token posts.

topics.title: There's an LLM in the Browser Now. Building With the Prompt API and Gemini Nano.
topics.whyTrending: Chrome 148 shipped the Prompt API to stable in May 2026 — Gemini Nano on-device with multimodal input and structured JSON output, three lines of JS, no API key, no server bill, no round trip. Chrome 149 expanded to five languages, and Gemma 197M now transparently powers task-specific APIs like summarizer on weaker hardware. Trip.com is already generating personalized summaries entirely client-side. A build-along with real availability detection, graceful degradation and honest latency numbers doesn't exist yet.
topics.gapNote: Only adjacent post is the edge-ai draft. Would finally give that draft a reason to ship.

topics.title: Two Years of Server Components: The Five Things Teams Consistently Get Wrong
topics.whyTrending: App Router passed Pages Router as the most common React setup for the first time, so RSC is now the majority path — but adoption is uneven and most failures trace to the same handful of mistakes: treating the server/client boundary as a rendering location rather than an execution boundary, pushing non-serializable props (functions, class instances, Date) across the wire, and expecting automatic performance wins that don't materialize. A postmortem-style piece with real failure modes beats another 'what are RSC' explainer.
topics.gapNote: Blog has RSC intro/comparison posts but no failure-mode postmortem. Strong internal-link hub.

topics.title: Baseline 2026: The CSS You Can Finally Ship Without a Fallback
topics.whyTrending: Container style queries, contrast-color(), the shape() function for clip-path and offset-path, the :open pseudo-class and custom highlights all reached Baseline Newly Available in 2026. shape() in particular replaces unreadable polygon() coordinate soup with move/line/curve commands that accept CSS units and math functions. Concrete, code-heavy, evergreen, and a genuine 'delete your fallback' moment rather than another 'CSS features you should know' listicle. Carried over from the 2026-08-16 session — still unpicked, still current.
topics.gapNote: Partially overlaps modern-css-2026-has-scope-container-queries — angle it as 'what changed since', not a rewrite.

topics.title: The Frontend System Design Interview in 2026: What They Actually Ask Now
topics.whyTrending: Listings are down ~35% from pre-2020 and ~70% from the 2022 peak, so interview loops got harder and more architectural — rendering strategy tradeoffs, caching layers, real-time sync, and increasingly 'how would you design this so agents can maintain it'. The blog already ranks with a deep JavaScript interview guide but has nothing on system design, which is the higher-intent, higher-volume sibling query and pulls steady traffic year-round.
topics.gapNote: Evergreen traffic anchor. Internal-links to BFF, micro-frontends, monorepo, performance-budgets, SSR strategies.

topics.title: Junior Hiring Is Down 67%. The Panic Is Aimed at the Wrong Thing.
topics.whyTrending: Entry-level developer hiring dropped 67% since 2022 and Google and Meta are taking ~50% fewer new grads than in 2021 — while AI engineer roles grew 300% and overall dev postings are up 15% since mid-2025. The market bifurcated rather than collapsed: enterprises, defense, finance and healthcare tech keep hiring juniors because compliance and legacy codebases demand human judgment; startups are the ones that cut. Devs use AI for ~60% of their work but can fully delegate only 0-20% of tasks. A data piece, not a hot take.
topics.gapNote: Adjacent to building-stronger-teams-by-empowering-junior-developers and ai-agents-not-replacing-developers-real-data — needs a distinct data-first framing.

topics.title: A Custom Video Player With Zero JavaScript State, Thanks to Chrome 152
topics.whyTrending: Chrome 152 shipped :playing, :paused, :seeking, :buffering, :stalled, :muted and :volume-locked — media state as CSS pseudo-classes, and an Interop 2026 focus area so the other engines are following. Every custom player today syncs state into class names with JavaScript event listeners; this deletes that layer entirely. Caveat worth being honest about: not Baseline yet, so the post needs a real progressive-enhancement path. A build-along with a working player and no state sync at all.
topics.gapNote: Carried from 2026-08-16, unpicked. Lowest score here — fun and linkable, but narrow search demand.
